newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes softer on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes softer on shortcovering.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,507-1,509 levs per dollar, softer from 1,502-1,505 in the morning due to shortcovering by several banks, which failed to place winning bids at T-bill auctions on Monday, dealers said.
Traders said foreign currency supply was also relatively high, which did not allow for the lev to drop further.
"The lev eased because at least two commercial banks were actively bidding for foreign currency to cover positions after Monday's sales on orders from clients," one dealer said.

He declined to name the banks but said they sold foreign currency for levs on orders from foreign investors willing to lock funds in high-yield, floating interest government securities at Monday's auctions.

Floater interest T-bill issues with maturities of six, nine and 12 months offered by the Finance ministry at auctions on Monday were heavily subscribed but the ministry approved only a part of the bids, aiming at a higher average accepted price.
Interest on the paper was set equal to the central bank main interest rate, now 5.2 percent monthly, and is adjusted each time the rate is changed.
"Today the banks had to buy back the foreign currency they sold on Monday after failing to place winning bids at the auctions," the dealer said.

Local and foreign investors have actively sold foreign currency for levs since March to invest in local debt instruments despite a gradual fall in the central bank main interest rate, which stood at 18 percent monthly in March.
Foreigners can invest in Bulgarian treasuries with maturity of six months or longer because only this type of government securities is considered a foreign investment under Bulgarian law.
"But if the main rate keeps falling we may see interest in local debt declining and foreign currency flowing out of the country," another dealer said.
